Triage: lands in `scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` + `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` (gate tooling) → `domain:devx`, type Bug, `pm:blocked`.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#6092

Rationale: the gate's own header documents the percent-encoding spelling as the worst of the family, yet a template-literal guard scans clean — declared gate behaviour ≠ enforced, in the silent-green direction. The tree is clean today (`process.argv[1]` in scripts is prose + one string payload only), so this is a gate hole, not an outage — no urgency premium.

Why blocked rather than queued: the fix shape already exists downstream (objectui PR #6133 — third `interpolation` array on `scanSource`, `comment`/`literal` unchanged so every existing caller keeps its mask), and its two load-bearing exclusions (the `${`/`}` brackets stay masked; a nested template's body stays masked) were bought with a measured mis-fire. Porting before that PR lands risks the same shared-helper diverging in shape across repos.

Unlock-action: when objectui#6092 closes, requeue and port the **landed** shape (including both pinned exclusions and their tests) — do not re-derive; verify the objectui final diff first, then adapt to this repo's callers (`run-with-stall-guard.mjs:607` string-payload reliance is the compatibility pin to preserve).

Claim: `domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`, branch `claude/issue-11838-interpolation-mask`.

## ⭐ `pm:blocked` cleared — the blocker's *reason* is discharged, though its literal target is still open

Triage blocked this with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#6092` and an unlock action reading "when objectui#6092 closes". **objectui#6092 is still open.** I am unblocking anyway, and the reasoning is the point:

The stated *rationale* for the block was not about the card. It was:

> the fix shape already exists downstream (objectui PR #6133 …) and its two load-bearing exclusions … were bought with a measured mis-fire. **Porting before that PR lands** risks the same shared-helper diverging in shape across repos.

The precondition is **PR #6133 landing**. It landed at 20:28:59Z — `merged: true`, merged by `yinlianghui-tw`. #6092 stays open only because #6133 was `Part of` it, PR **1 of 2**; PR 2 is the conversion of objectui's 29 hand-typed guards to `isEntrypoint`, which touches call sites and cannot move `scanSource`'s shape at all. So waiting on #6092 would be waiting on work that has no bearing on what this card ports.

Verified by content on objectui `origin/main`, not from the PR body:

| reading | result |
|:---|:---|
| landing commit, located by `(#6133)` in its subject | `0c25598 feat(tooling): gate scripts/ entry guards on one predicate (#6133)` |
| `interpolation` array present in `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` | yes — `const interpolation = new Uint8Array(n)` at `:150`, with the brace-balancing at `:271-277` and the documented-contract note at `:290` |
| `scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` exists there | yes, 995 lines |
| **control** — `ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS`, which #6133 says it deliberately did *not* port | **0** |

That control is what makes the three positive readings trustworthy: the grep discriminates rather than matching everything.

⚠️ Worth recording for the `Blocked-by:` machinery itself: this card's real precondition was *"a PR merges"*, and the field can only name an issue — so it named the tracking card and would have parked this for work that was never the dependency. That is precisely the shape #11220 measures. I am not fixing it here; adding the instance.

## Pre-dispatch collision check

Surface: `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` + `scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs`. Across the union of all open PR branches and in-flight dev branches, both are claimed **0** times (`js-comment-mask` 0, `check-entry-guard` 0, `invoked-as` 0), against a live control — the same scan returns 1 for `check-engine-double-contract`, 1 for `check-platform-checklist`, 1 for `check-type-check-coverage`, 2 for `guard-shared-stash`.

⚠️ **But the semantic radius is much larger than the file radius, and larger than it was downstream.** 24 modules in this repo import `js-comment-mask`, several of which concurrent work is editing right now — `check-platform-checklist.mjs` (PR #11847, armed), `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `check-examples-live-imports.mjs` (in-flight #11511), `docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs` (in-flight #11434). The additive design is what makes this safe (`comment` and `literal` unchanged, so every existing caller keeps its mask), and that property is now load-bearing for four other pieces of in-flight work rather than merely tidy.

**Model tier: fable.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` at `a1c804bc9` reports no path-derived mandate — so this is judgment, and it goes to the ceiling for two reasons the downstream author did not face: the 24-consumer blast radius above, and the fact that **this repo has `scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`**, the corpus sweep #6133 explicitly declined to port. That gate exists only here, it will judge this port, and nothing downstream had to satisfy it.

Dispatching now.
